US-119-HR10938.description: To amend title 38, United States Code, to increase the maximum amount of a home health service benefit available to certain veterans under the laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.

US-119-HR10916.title: Aquatic Restoration and Conservation Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources, and in addition to the Committee on Agriculture, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10916.description: To require the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of the Interior to jointly develop a strategy to increase the use of aquatic restoration and conservation activities in wildfire risk mitigation and post-fire recovery efforts, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10916.aiSummary: The bill would require the Agriculture and Interior secretaries to make a joint plan to expand the use of aquatic restoration and conservation in wildfire risk work and post-fire recovery on federal lands. It would look at science, staff training, and ways to use these efforts in fuel reduction projects, grant-funded work, contracts, and stewardship agreements. The plan would be due within 1 year after enactment, and the secretaries would then send a report to Congress.

US-119-HR1721.title: Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act
US-119-HR1721.summary:
Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act

This bill requires the Department of Commerce to study and report on products that are in high demand across the critical infrastructure sectors. Critical infrastructure sectors are those whose assets, systems, and networks are vital to national security, the economy, public health or safety, or any combination of those matters.

The study must (1) identify the products in high demand across those sectors that are being imported due to manufacturing, material, or supply chain constraints; and (2) analyze the costs, benefits, and feasibility of manufacturing those products in the United States.
US-119-HR1721.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-02-27)

US-119-HR10839.title: Heat Island Reduction Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10839.description: To reduce the heat island effect and associated ground level ozone pollution from Federal facilities, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10839.aiSummary: The bill would require federal agencies to make plans to reduce heat buildup at federal properties and facilities in areas with ozone pollution problems. The plans would look at steps like adding trees, shade, cool roofs, and cooler paving, and would also include costs, timelines, and funding. Agencies would update the plans every 2 years, and the General Services Administration would report yearly to Congress on progress.

US-119-HR10817.title: U.S.S. Doris Miller Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10817.description: To express the sense of Congress regarding the naming of a naval aircraft carrier for Mess Attendant Third Class Doris "Dorie" Miller, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10817.aiSummary: The bill would state that Congress thinks the Navy should name an aircraft carrier the "Doris Miller" to honor Mess Attendant Third Class Doris "Dorie" Miller. It gives a short history of Miller’s service at Pearl Harbor, where he saved his captain, fired an anti-aircraft gun, and helped evacuate sailors. The bill was introduced in the House and sent to the House Armed Services Committee.

US-119-HR10718.title: Federal Employee Records Relief Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10718.description: To establish a temporary process for former Federal employees to obtain personnel records, secure administrative corrections to personnel and benefits documentation, and receive benefits coordination support, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10718.aiSummary: The bill would create a temporary way for former federal workers to ask for their personnel records, fix missing or wrong personnel and benefits papers, and get help with benefits coverage details. It applies to people who left federal jobs on or after January 20, 2025, and they could make requests for 4 years after the bill becomes law. Federal offices would have to help find and share the needed records.

US-119-S5656.title: Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5656.description: A bill to amend title 18, United States Code, to provide for victims of crime to be notified of firearms-related activity by the offender, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5656.aiSummary: The bill would create an FBI-run notice system for crime victims who register, so they can get alerts about certain firearm-related actions by the offender. It would also let legal guardians or other lawful representatives sign up for minors or incapacitated victims. The bill would set up a pilot program for states and tribes with victim notice systems to get reports about firearm check denials and status changes in some domestic violence cases.

US-119-S5579.title: Mapping Housing Discrimination Act
committees: Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5579.description: A bill to authorize a grant program for educational institutions to analyze, digitize, and map historic records relating to housing information, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5579.aiSummary: The bill would create a grant program for colleges and other eligible schools to analyze, digitize, and map old records about housing discrimination in at least one local area. It would also direct the Department of Housing and Urban Development to set data rules and build a free public national database from the project data. US-119-S5557.description: A bill to establish in the National Institute of Standards and Technology a program of measurement research, and for other purposes.

US-119-HR5109.title: Transportation Worker Identification Credential Efficiency Act
US-119-HR5109.summary:
This bill directs the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to develop guidelines to improve access to a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) for prisoners prior to their release.

Specifically, TSA must develop guidelines to assist individuals in federal, state, and local prisons in (1) pre-applying or preparing an application for a TWIC card; and (2) requesting an appeal or waiver of a preliminary determination of ineligibility for a TWIC card.

As background, a TWIC card is required by the Maritime Transportation Security Act for workers who need access to secure areas of U.S. maritime facilities and vessels. TSA conducts a background check to determine a person’s eligibility and issues the credential.
US-119-HR5109.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-09-03)

US-119-HR1501.title: Protecting Domestic Mining Act of 2025
US-119-HR1501.summary:
Protecting Domestic Mining Act of 2025

This bill provides statutory authority for federal agencies to expedite the environmental review of certain mining infrastructure projects.

Specifically, the bill permanently makes certain mining infrastructure projects eligible for expedited environmental review under the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act (FAST Act). This provides statutory authority for similar authorities that were included in the rule titled Adding Mining as a Sector of Projects Eligible for Coverage Under Title 41 of the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act and issued by the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council (Permitting Council) on January 8, 2021.

The bill also prohibits the Permitting Council from finalizing its proposed rule titled Revising Scope of the Mining Sector of Projects That Are Eligible for Coverage Under Title 41 of the Fixing America’s Surface Transportation Act and issued on September 22, 2023. Among other modifications, the rule proposes to limit the types of mining projects that are eligible for the expedited environmental review process. Specifically, the proposed rule limits the expedited process to critical minerals mining projects.

US-119-S5238.title: For Our Republic Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5238.description: A bill to preserve the democratic republic of the United States from the overreach of authoritarian tactics.
US-119-S5238.aiSummary: The bill would make a wide set of changes to federal government rules, including limits on how agencies can be reorganized and rules for independent inspectors general and civil service layoffs. It would also bar Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection from using biometric surveillance tools, and would add new limits and protections for noncitizen children in custody. Other parts would address election media made by AI, federal spending, ethics rules, and law enforcement at polls.

US-119-HR5549.title: Efficient Nuclear Licensing Hearings Act
US-119-HR5549.summary:
Efficient Nuclear Licensing Hearings Act

This bill expedites the process of reviewing certain uncontested permits and licenses for nuclear power plants (e.g., construction permits and operating licenses) by removing a requirement for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to hold a public hearing at the end of the process. The bill applies to the licenses and permits if a hearing has not been requested by a person whose interest may be affected. The bill also directs the NRC to use informal adjudicatory procedures if such a hearing is held.

Additionally, the bill directs the NRC to hold an adjudicatory hearing regarding the licensing of the construction and operation of a uranium enrichment facility only if the person whose interest may be affected by such construction and operation has requested the hearing.
US-119-HR5549.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-09-23)

US-119-S1157.title: Women and Lung Cancer Research and Preventive Services Act of 2025
US-119-S1157.summary:
Women and Lung Cancer Research and Preventive Services Act of 2025

This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services to conduct an interagency review to accelerate lung cancer research, prevention, and awareness with respect to women and underserved populations.

The review must
• report on the status of existing research and current knowledge gaps;
• identify new opportunities for collaborative research to determine the causes of lung cancer and advance prevention, screening, diagnosis, and treatment; and
• provide recommendations for a national lung cancer screening strategy and public education campaign.

US-119-HJRES140.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to Public Land Order No. 7917 for Withdrawal of Federal Lands; Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis Counties, MN.
US-119-HJRES140.summary: This joint resolution opens approximately 225,504 acres of National Forest System lands in Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis Counties in Minnesota to mineral and geothermal leasing. Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies Public Land Order 7917 , which withdrew such land from mineral and geothermal leasing for 20 years beginning in 2023. The Bureau of Land Management issued the order to protect and preserve the Rainy River Watershed, the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness, the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness Mining Protection Area, and the 1854 Ceded Territory of the Lake Superior Chippewa from potential adverse effects of mineral and geothermal exploration and development. The joint resolution removes such protections and allows such land to be leased for the exploration and development of minerals and geothermal energy.
